```{r, reading in data file}
cort<-read.csv("Nestling.CORT.2017.csv")
```

```{r, filtering out BHCO nestlings}
cort<-cort%>%
  filter(bhco.nestling %in% c("no"))
```

```{r, turning data into real date}
#turn all your date column into a real date
cort$Date = as.Date(cort$Date, "%m/%d/%y")
cort$Date

#Create "day" column for julian date for analysis
cort$day.of.year=yday(cort$Date)
#use day from now on!!!!!!!

#mean center by total (day)
cort$mean.cent.day<-(cort$day)-(mean(cort$day))
```

```{r, cort between habitat types}

#Make summary table
cort.sum<-summarySE(cort, measurevar="Baseline.cort", groupvars=c("Habitat"), na.rm = T)

#Make figure
Fig.1<-ggplot(cort, aes(x=Habitat, y=Baseline.cort, color = Habitat)) +
  geom_boxplot(coef = 5, width= 0.5) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.3, dodge.width = 0.9), size=1, stroke=2) +
  geom_point(stat = 'summary', fun = mean, shape = '+', size = 6,
             color = 'blue', position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  xlab("Habitat") +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(panel.grid.major =element_blank(), panel.grid.minor =element_blank())+
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 15))) +
  ylab("Baseline cort (ng/mL)")+
  guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Habitat"))+
  scale_color_taylor(palette = "lover")
Fig.1

#create a tiff image for presentations/pubs
dev.off()
jpeg(file='CORT.no.bhco.jpeg', width = 8, height = 6, units = 'in',res=800)
Fig.1 + theme(legend.position="none")
dev.off() ##parentheses empty
```

```{r, fig. 2}

habitat_colors <- c("Urban" = "grey60", "Rural" = "green4")

# Habitat x Day interaction p-value, computed from your data
fit <- lm(Baseline.cort ~ Habitat * Day, data = cort)
p_int <- anova(fit)["Habitat:Day", "Pr(>F)"]

fig.2 <- ggplot(cort, aes(x = Day, y = Baseline.cort, color = Habitat, fill = Habitat)) +

  # Regression lines + CI bands first, so points sit on top
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", se = TRUE,
    alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.9,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # Black-outlined points, jittered horizontally only
  geom_point(
    shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.4,
    size = 2.5, alpha = 0.9,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, seed = 1)
  ) +

  annotate(
    "text", x = Inf, y = -Inf,
    label = paste0("Habitat \u00d7 Day: p = ", sprintf("%.3f", p_int)),
    hjust = 1.05, vjust = -1,
    fontface = "italic", color = "grey40", size = 4
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = habitat_colors, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_color_manual(values = habitat_colors, name = "Habitat") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 5:10) +

  labs(x = "Nestling age (days)", y = "Baseline corticosterone (ng/mL)") +

  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.18, 0.85),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.background = element_blank()
  )

fig.2

#create a tiff image for presentations/pubs
dev.off()
jpeg(file='CORT.no.bhco.trends.jpeg', width = 8, height = 6, units = 'in',res=800)
fig.2 + theme(legend.position="right")
dev.off() ##parentheses empty
```

```{r, cort between habitat types}

#log transforming data
cort$t.cort<-log(cort$Baseline.cort)

lmm.1<-lmer(t.cort~Habitat+mean.cent.day+Day+(1|NID), data=cort)

#checking to see the contribution of NID to variation in cort... less than 1%
lmm.7<-lmer(t.cort~1+(1|NID), data=cort)

#Summary plots for the model
check_model(lmm.1)

hist(residuals(lmm.1))

shapiro.test(residuals(lmm.1))

summary(lmm.7)
#No real effects here, other than on day but keeping age because it varies so much in the birds we sampled
plot(allEffects(lmm.1))

res.pro.table <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(lmm.1)))
#write.csv(res.pro.table,"3.5.26.nestling.cort.results.csv")

```
